note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Card, fact: 'Free elections were not held there' is an overgeneralisation. Some fairly free elections did take place, such as Hungary in 1945 and Czechoslovakia in 1946, before communist takeovers. Poland's 1947 election was rigged. Wording such as 'free elections were not held or were rigged in most countries' would be accurate.
- Card, wording: 'Agreed that Germany would be defeated' is odd, since defeat was not something the leaders could agree on. What they agreed at Yalta was Germany's unconditional surrender.

rejected.title: Yalta and Potsdam
card: In 1945 the Allied leaders met twice to plan the end of the war and postwar Europe. Yalta was in February, in the Crimea. Potsdam was in July and August, near Berlin, after Germany had surrendered.
At Yalta, Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin agreed that Germany would be defeated and split into zones run by the Allies. Stalin promised free elections in Eastern Europe.
At Potsdam, Truman, Stalin and Churchill (later replaced by Attlee) confirmed the zones and moved Poland's borders west. Germany's capital, Berlin, was also divided into zones.
Disagreements grew. Soviet forces stayed in Eastern Europe and free elections were not held there. The Western leaders came to distrust Stalin's promises, and Stalin distrusted them.
rejected.remember: The conferences planned postwar Europe, but broken promises and clashing aims fed distrust.

a.q: Which agreement was made about Germany at Yalta and Potsdam?
opts: It would be divided into zones run by the Allies
It would be joined to Poland as one state
It would be run by the Soviet Union alone
It would be left free to rule itself at once
a.why: The Allies agreed to divide Germany into zones, and Berlin was split too. Soviet control of all Germany is wrong, because the Western Allies ran zones as well.
a.clue: Think about who ran each part of Germany.

b.q: Why did the Yalta and Potsdam conferences add to Cold War distrust?
opts: The free elections promised for the east were not held
Germany was left united and armed after the war
Stalin refused to attend the Potsdam conference
The Western leaders agreed to give up their zones
b.why: Stalin had promised free elections in Eastern Europe, but Soviet forces stayed and the elections were not held. The West saw this as a broken promise. Stalin did attend Potsdam, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Look at what Stalin promised and what then happened.
